identity.title: Mixing for Dynamical Systems Driven by Stationary Noises

problems.title: Infinite-dimensional noise regularity does not transfer as asserted
problems.claim: Summed L1 continuity of coordinate conditional densities does not give a common TV-Lipschitz bound; identical spatial copies need not preserve TV continuity; the literal compact support of a continuous finite-fiber density on all of infinite-dimensional E is impossible.
problems.all_hypotheses: A: E=l2; r_l=4^-l; independent stationary chains with invariant f(x)=3(1-x^2)/4 on [-1,1] and kernel f(y)(1+2^-l*x*y). Full past support, positive summable r_l, bounded scalar paths, each scaled coordinate density jointly Lipschitz, summed L1 continuity by dominated convergence, eta2 by finite-coordinate minorization and deterministic tail. B: bounded trigonometric basis, summable sup-norm coefficients, g=1+alpha*clip(first past coefficient)*clip(first next coefficient), scalar SF and recurrence, iid spatial copies with b_j=2^-j. B obeys the construction conditions and natural finite-fiber interpretation, NOT the impossible literal global compact-support clause.
problems.decisive_proof: A: pasts differing at time zero in coordinate l by +/-r_l have distance 2r_l while the event next lth coordinate positive has probability gap 3*2^-l/8. Ratio at least 3*2^l/16 diverges. B: past distance 2*c1*b_j tends to zero but the same coordinate event gap is 3*alpha/8 independent of j, so TV continuity fails. C: a nonzero continuous function supported in compact K would give an open ball inside K; an infinite-dimensional compact set has empty interior, forcing rho_n=0 and contradicting conditional normalization.
problems.counterreadings: These are not counterexamples to Theorem 3.4 with all its explicitly assumed SF hypotheses. The literal DLP-prime problem is acknowledged, not silently repaired when claiming B satisfies hypotheses. Example A alone meets the actual eta1/eta2 clauses. Amplitude decay does not reduce TV distances of rescaled distinguishable scalar laws. B uses bounded time paths, so NS scalar boundedness does not remove it.
problems.actual_impact: Core advertised noise-to-theorem and infinite-product application steps fail. The general correlated product justification in the NS proof is unsupported; conditional abstract theorem and all individual PDE mixing conclusions are not declared false.
problems.severity_reason: A failed central hypothesis transfer directly affects core applications; no whole-paper refutation is needed.
problems.repair: Assume/prove SF directly for a narrower class or require a quantitative summed scaled coordinate TV-Lipschitz bound. Reformulate DLP-prime support in finite fibers while maintaining actual conditional measure support K. Identical nontrivial memory spatial products require a different noise class or a weaker-metric coupling.
problems.repair_limits: The support wording repair does not cure A or B. No complete revised PDE theorem is claimed.
problems.independent_calculation: Exact density moments and event/distance ratios actually executed; analytic infinite-dimensional proof is decisive.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: eta1 p.5 and history metric p.4; SF p.16; DLP-prime p.28 and claimed implication p.29; Propositions 4.7/4.9/4.10 pp.41-43; application pp.48-49.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: For f=3(1-x^2)/4 on [-1,1], the kernels f(y)(1+2^-l*x*y) are positive, normalized and invariant for f. Scaling by r_l=4^-l gives a compact Hilbert box and summable radii. Each fixed coordinate density is jointly Lipschitz; its L1 change is (3 a_l/8)|Delta xi_l/r_l|, bounded by a summable multiple of a_l. Full past support follows from positive finite cylinders; finite-coordinate minorization plus a deterministic tail proves eta2.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Time-zero pasts +/-r_l have metric distance 2r_l and next-coordinate positive-event probability gap 3 a_l/8, hence variation/distance >=3*2^l/16. No common SF Lipschitz constant exists. For identical correlated spatial copies with coefficient b_j, scalar bounded trigonometric series and g=1+alpha chi(xi_0)chi(y) satisfy the construction's quantitative positivity and scalar regularity; distance 2 c_1 b_j tends to zero but event gap 3 alpha/8 persists. A continuous density on all of infinite-dimensional E supported in compact K must vanish identically, contradicting the literal DLP-prime normalization.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The product example is not falsely claimed to satisfy the impossible literal DLP-prime support clause. The eta1 example independently refutes the explicit p.29 implication. Bounded scalar paths in the spatial example satisfy the additional NS boundedness requirement. Rescaling amplitudes leaves coordinate-law distinguishability unchanged.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: Theorem 3.4 explicitly requires SF. The general correlated product justification in Theorem 5.4 invokes Proposition 4.10 without proving SF; this is a central hypothesis-transfer gap.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Major is warranted by a demonstrated failure of a core application step; no falsity of the conditional abstract theorem or every PDE mixing conclusion is asserted.
independent_acceptance.repair_limits: Finite-fiber support wording fixes the empty-interior contradiction only. Direct SF assumptions or a quantitatively controlled narrower noise model are needed; amplitude decay alone and summed continuity do not supply them.

problems.title: No common continuous-time compact invariant set under the stated window-energy bound
problems.claim: Proposition 5.1's compact set, invariant under every control satisfying (5.3) for every t>=0, need not exist.
problems.all_hypotheses: n=2, V=(q1^2+q2^2)/2, gamma1=gamma2=1. Two independent stable oscillators with smooth coercive V. For A=[[0,1],[-1,-1]], positive P=[[3/2,1/2],[1/2,1]] has A^T P+P A=-I. Lyapunov convolution establishes BAS for every M and every initial bounded ball. The free flow converges exponentially uniformly on every bounded set, satisfying the global stability intended by SE on any proposed compact X.
problems.decisive_proof: For any nonempty compact X choose a point maximizing p1. With M=1, let A0=1+|p1*|+|q1*| and forcing zeta1=A0 on [0,1/(2*A0^2)], zero thereafter, zeta2=0. All unit-window energies are <=1/2, but p1'(0+)=A0-q1*-p1*>0; the trajectory leaves X immediately. Thus no such common invariant set exists.
problems.counterreadings: The stronger pointwise bound (1.12) is expressly a stronger sufficient condition on p44, not the Prop5.1 hypothesis. Integer-time invariance is weaker than its all-time assertion. Empty X cannot satisfy absorption. SE is stated using the claimed X, but the example has the stronger uniform free stability on every bounded set.
problems.actual_impact: False lemma supports the compact-state reduction and the domain of LC in the ODE mixing proof. General final integer-time mixing has not been disproved.
problems.severity_reason: Central application reduction uses a false invariant-set assertion; repair requires changing state-space construction or hypotheses.
problems.repair: Use aligned unit-block concatenation and BAS at budget 2M to construct an integer-time invariant set, rechecking compactness and LC; or impose a suitable pointwise forcing bound. Uniform attraction on a compact set should give GCP directly, not be identified with global norm contraction GD on all H.
problems.repair_limits: No claim that the proposed discrete-time repair proves a fully revised author theorem. Concatenated budget-M controls can create a budget-2M window.
problems.independent_calculation: Exact rational Lyapunov identity and positive definiteness plus pulse-energy checks executed; analytic maximum-coordinate proof is decisive.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: ODE (5.1) p.43; BAS/(5.3), SE and Proposition 5.1 pp.44-45; LC and Theorem 5.2 p.46.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: n=2, both endpoint damping coefficients one, V=(q1^2+q2^2)/2 is smooth and coercive. A=[[0,1],[-1,-1]] and P=[[3/2,1/2],[1/2,1]] satisfy A^T P+P A=-I with P positive. L'<=-L/(2 lambda_max(P))+(5/2)|zeta|^2 proves BAS for every energy budget. The free flow decays exponentially uniformly on every bounded set, stronger than the intended SE.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: For any nonempty compact candidate X select a maximizer of p1. A0=1+|p1*|+|q1*|, duration 1/(2 A0^2), zeta1=A0 and zeta2=0 give every sliding-window energy <=1/2<1, yet p1'(0+)=A0-q1*-p1*>0. This immediately leaves X. Absorption excludes an empty candidate.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The pointwise bound is explicitly called stronger on p.44 and is not assumed in Proposition 5.1. The claim quantifies over all real t>=0, not only aligned integer blocks. SE uses the proposed X circularly, but the example satisfies free stability on every bounded set.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: The p.45 reachable-set proof concatenates controls without preserving the budget of windows crossing the join; the asserted X is then used in LC and the Theorem 5.2 reduction.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: The false compact-state reduction is a Major proof dependency even though no counterexample to the final integer-time mixing conclusion is established.
independent_acceptance.repair_limits: Aligned blocks with BAS at budget 2M may support a different discrete-time construction; compactness and LC still need verification. Compact uniform attraction is not the global norm contraction GD on all H.

problems.title: Square-summable L2 basis coefficients do not imply bounded time paths
problems.claim: The stated basis and coefficient hypotheses permit almost surely unbounded trajectories inside one unit block.
problems.all_hypotheses: Dyadic intervals I_j=(2^-j,2^(1-j)); odd basis functions 2^(j/2)*1_Ij, even basis completes all zero-mean interval subspaces. Odd radii 2^(-j/4), even radii 2^-j; all positive and square summable. Independent scaled Lipschitz f densities and g=1 give precisely the stated coefficient/kernel construction with compact L2 support.
problems.decisive_proof: The average on I_j is zeta_(2j-1)*2^(j/2). Independent events |zeta|>=radius/2 have probability 5/16. Infinitely many averages exceed 2^(j/4)/2 almost surely, excluding an L-infinity representative. Zero-mean other coefficients cannot cancel these averages.
problems.counterreadings: Uniform L2 boundedness and compact support hold; they do not bound timewise values. This construction is not falsely asserted to meet the impossible literal DLP-prime density support clause.
problems.actual_impact: Local bounded-path claim false. NS separately imposes scalar paths bounded by one and excludes this example; no independent NS theorem failure follows from P3.
problems.severity_reason: A local excess regularity assertion has a direct stronger-coefficient repair already enforced separately in the principal bounded-forcing application.
problems.repair: Require sum c_l*||phi_l||_infinity finite or another justified bound on the random series.
problems.repair_limits: No assertion that arbitrary square-summable coefficients suffice after only redefining representatives.
problems.independent_calculation: Exact probability 5/16 and sample lower-bound growth executed; Borel-Cantelli/interval-average proof is decisive.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: General L2 basis and square-summable coefficient assumptions p.41; bounded-trajectory assertions pp.42-43.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: The dyadic normalized indicators are orthonormal; adjoining bases of each interval's zero-mean subspace completes L2. Odd radii 2^(-j/4) and even radii 2^-j are square summable. Independent scaled f densities are compactly supported and Lipschitz, and g=1 satisfies the stated construction inputs.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The interval average equals zeta_(2j-1)*2^(j/2), since every other basis member integrates to zero there. Independent events of probability 5/16 force averages >=2^(j/4)/2 in absolute value infinitely often. No essentially bounded representative can have these averages, despite compact L2 support.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The example concerns the actual basis/coefficient inputs, not the impossible literal global density-support clause. Navier-Stokes separately requires scalar paths bounded by one and excludes it.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: This is a local excess time-regularity claim in the noise construction; it does not independently refute the bounded-forcing PDE application.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Minor remains appropriate because a justified uniform series bound, e.g. sum c_l||phi_l||_infinity<infinity, removes this local overstatement.
independent_acceptance.repair_limits: Changing representatives does not remedy divergent interval averages.

problems.title: Stationary solution need not have the strong-feeble property (4.11)
problems.claim: Uniform dual-Lipschitz trajectory convergence does not imply the supremum over all continuous tests bounded by one in (4.11).
problems.all_hypotheses: H=l2, E=R, a=1/2, R right shift, S(u,eta)=eta*e1+a*R*u; X={|u_j|<=a^(j-1)} compact invariant. Smooth bounded-on-bounded derivatives; GD immediate; ALC with G=span(e1), complementary derivative norm a and onto noise derivative. IID density f has SF=0, literal DLP-prime with F_n=R and compactly supported Lipschitz density f, and SRZ.
problems.decisive_proof: Stationary u_k=(eta_k,a*eta_(k-1),...). Given past through zero, coordinate k+1 equals a^k*u0,1 deterministically. A continuous bump of width epsilon*a^k around that value has conditional expectation 1 and stationary expectation <=3epsilon/2. Supremum in (4.11) is >=1 for every k, so cannot tend to zero.
problems.counterreadings: The test may depend on k and the chosen past because the displayed supremum permits it. Noise SF does not imply state-process SF. Synchronous coupling still gives exponential dual-Lipschitz convergence; no contradiction to Proposition3.7 as actually stated.
problems.actual_impact: The isolated total-variation-strengthening sentence fails; the main weaker mixing conclusion survives.
problems.severity_reason: Local corollary overstatement outside the main dual-Lipschitz theorem.
problems.repair: Retain feeble/dual-Lipschitz mixing or prove additional state-space total-variation regularization.
problems.repair_limits: No inference of state SF from iid noise and no full-total-variation theorem claimed.
problems.independent_calculation: Exact bump-expectation bounds executed; deterministic retained-coordinate proof is decisive.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: Theorem 3.4 assumptions pp.27-29, Proposition 3.7 p.33 and (4.11)/following sentence p.39.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: S(u,eta)=eta e1+(1/2)Ru on H=l2 with finite E=R is smooth, globally contractive at zero, and has determining G=span(e1) with exact noise controllability. The invariant Hilbert box is compact. Iid f noise has SF constant zero, genuine finite-dimensional compact density support with F_n=E, and SRZ.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: In the stationary solution, conditional on its past, coordinate k+1 at time k is deterministically a^k(u0)_1. A continuous bump of width epsilon*a^k around this value has conditional expectation one and unconditional expectation <=3 epsilon/2. The allowed supremum over all sup-norm-bounded continuous tests is therefore >=1 for every k.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The test is allowed to depend on k and the chosen past; there is no Lipschitz-constant bound in (4.11). The state process need not inherit the noise's SF. Synchronous coupling still gives exponential dual-Lipschitz contraction.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: The overstatement is the later strong-feeble corollary, not Proposition 3.7's actual dual-Lipschitz convergence.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Minor local strengthening error; the main weaker mixing conclusion survives.
independent_acceptance.repair_limits: Retain the weaker mixing claim or add genuine state-space variation regularization; no such strengthening follows from iid noise alone.

clarifications_and_rejected_candidates.reason: Same middle marginal and TV triangle term directly verified in v3; primary gluing hypotheses checked.
Upper semicontinuity and finite cover supply uniform approximation.
Finite-dimensional coordinatewise extension costs a constant absorbed by smallness.
Earlier k-star contraction time restores finite-step access; no separate theorem failure claimed.

limitations: No counterexample to Theorem3.4 with all its printed hypotheses is asserted.
No proof that every affected PDE or the final integer-time ODE mixing conclusion is false.
Literal infinite-dimensional DLP-prime support is impossible; product examples are not falsely claimed to satisfy that clause.
Selected gluing dependency checked; other cited monographs and PDE regularity results not fully independently reproved.
Exact author manuscript only; no VoR equivalence; no author code run or unseen supplement checked.
repair_verification: Local analytical repairs and scope limits were examined. P1 requires genuinely stronger noise regularity. P2 discrete-time construction is an outlined route, not a completed revised theorem. No author adoption.
independent_acceptance_scope: Independent verification of every reported Problem P1-P4, including literal hypotheses, counterexamples, central application dependencies and severity. Historical whole-source reading, v2/v3 gluing comparison and external PDE/reference checks remain attributed to the initial review; they are not newly certified here.
